trust_decision.summary: Whether the request's client address is trustworthy: Flask decides the caller identity used for API rate limiting, API-key/login audit logging and the Click'N'Load loopback gate from an unvalidated client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header (helpers.py:360, helpers.py:449, app_blueprint.py:86) or the raw WSGI REMOTE_ADDR (cnl_blueprint.py:33), so the client chooses its own audit-log identity and rate-limit bucket.

landing_point.why: The advisory title leads with rate-limit bypass, and this is the single line where the rate_limit decorator takes its bucket key straight from X-Forwarded-For (first element, falling back to remote_addr); a grep for X-Forwarded-For lands here and at the two sibling reads in helpers.py:360 and app_blueprint.py:86.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP GET/POST /api/<func> via @apikey_auth (api_blueprint.py:24); client IP is written into the API-key success/failure audit lines helpers.py:386 and helpers.py:393
HTTP POST /login (app_blueprint.py:75-111); client IP is written into the login success/failure audit lines app_blueprint.py:90 and app_blueprint.py:95
reached from cnl_blueprint.py:39 (is_loopback_request(check_source=False) fallback inside local_check)

application construction: App.__new__ builds the Flask app and is called from WebServerThread.__init__ (src/pyload/webui/webserver_thread.py:32); the fix wraps app.wsgi_app in ProxyFix here (fix.diff:33-40, fix.diff:48)
config load/merge: ConfigParser.read_default_config (src/pyload/core/config/parser.py:106-120) exposes webui/trusted_proxies, read once at app construction (fix.diff:13)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Click'N'Load's loopback gate is a separate feature in another blueprint that never reads X-Forwarded-For (it compares the raw WSGI REMOTE_ADDR with g.web_addr), so the XFF rate-limit/audit-log advisory does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink. (a) A deployment behind a configured trusted reverse proxy must still resolve the real client from the XFF hop, so per-client rate-limit buckets and audit-log IPs stay correct - an over-broad 'never look at X-Forwarded-For' fix makes every client behind the proxy share one bucket and logs the proxy address (the fix's own test at fix.diff:314-348 pins this). (b) The Click'N'Load loopback gate must keep testing the pre-middleware TCP peer - installing ProxyFix without reading werkzeug.proxy_fix.orig lets a remote client send 'X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1' and satisfy local_addr == remote_addr.

O6_input_shapes: X-Forwarded-For with a comma-separated multi-hop chain, where only the trusted hop count from the right may be used (ProxyFix x_for=N)
no X-Forwarded-For header at all (fall back to the TCP peer address)
X-Forwarded-For present while trusted_proxies is 0, i.e. the default: header must be ignored entirely
negative trusted_proxies value (rejected with ValueError at app construction)
REMOTE_ADDR absent/None (pinned code fails open in rate_limit; fixed code falls back to the constant 'unknown')
the pre-middleware REMOTE_ADDR after ProxyFix has rewritten it (werkzeug.proxy_fix.orig), needed by the loopback checks

O7_producer.where: src/pyload/core/config/parser.py:106-120 (ConfigParser.read_default_config parses PKGDIR default.cfg and merges the user's saved settings/pyload.cfg over it; the value is declared at src/pyload/core/config/default.cfg:47-48 and cast to int by parser.py:259-264)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-client rate limit or client-IP audit entry on the /json/* endpoints, which today have @login_required but no IP-based throttle
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same webui package as the fixed /api route; the rate_limit decorator already exists and json_blueprint is the sibling browser-facing API, so a maintainer adding abuse protection would plausibly add it here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the Click'N'Load socket proxy logging or forwarding a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP to the backend instead of the socket peer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a reverse proxy in front of the same Flask app (ClickNLoad.py:281 connects to web_addr and forwards the raw request), so 'preserve the original client' is a natural and wrong enhancement for it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-client failed-login counter/lockout inside check_auth, keyed by an address the webui passes in
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: check_auth is where authentication actually happens and is called from the login view and the API; a maintainer could add brute-force protection there instead of in the webui decorators, in the core package where the config lives.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: installing ProxyFix on the PathInfoDispatcher WSGI app instead of on app.wsgi_app
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two serving paths already exist (flask app.run in develop, cheroot PathInfoDispatcher in production), so a second middleware composition point is easy to imagine.

O9_family: CWE-290 Authentication Bypass by Spoofing - client-controlled X-Forwarded-For trusted as the client identity (rate-limit bypass and audit-log spoofing; additionally, enabling ProxyFix without preserving the pre-middleware peer would open the Click'N'Load loopback gate)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools + setup.cfg (pip install -e .[test]); pytest with testpaths=tests (setup.cfg:114-137); no lockfile; runtime deps from setup.cfg:65-87 include Flask (brings Werkzeug, which supplies werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix), Flask-Session, Flask-WTF, Flask-Caching, Cheroot, cryptography, pycurl and mini-racer (the last two need system libs at build time)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/test_api_rate_limit.py (rate_limit incl. XFF; note lines 198-236 at the pinned commit assert the vulnerable XFF-trust behaviour and are rewritten by the fix), tests/integration/test_cnl.py (CNL local gate through the Flask test client, fixture at tests/integration/conftest.py:36-38), tests/unit/test_check_ipv6_transitions.py (is_loopback_address). The test methods the fix adds (get_client_ip, trusted proxies, ProxyFix) are absent from the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep trusting the header but sanitise it - take the last hop or strip private/loopback values - or simply reject requests carrying X-Forwarded-For, instead of removing header trust from the three consumers and adding a configurable trusted-proxy hop count resolved by ProxyFix.

out_of_scope_notes: The Click'N'Load addon's socket proxy (src/pyload/plugins/addons/ClickNLoad.py:210-281) accepts connections from any host when hosts_filter is empty and forwards them to the loopback web backend, so the blueprint's local gate sees a loopback peer; that is a separate, documented 'Insecure! Use at your own risk!!!' feature (ClickNLoad.py:22), not header-based, and I did not pursue it.
